content.text:
Chamber C's etch rate jumped after its overnight PM. Edge ring replacement and wet clean (PM-C-1126) ended at 01:40, and from the first lot back (N2-0811) the rate ran high, at 51.9–53.8 nm/min against a centre of 50.0 and an upper limit of 53.0. Two runs broke the upper limit (runs 25 and 30) and run 27 tripped the two-sigma rule. Runs 1–22 before the PM stayed between 49.2 and 51.1.

All eight lots that ran after the PM (N2-0811 to N2-0818, 200 wafers) are on hold. The sort test found edge-ring failures in five of the eight lots sampled. Lots N2-0811 and N2-0812 had no edge-ring failures in their samples but are still on hold with the rest.

What to look at next:
- The edge ring installed in PM-C-1126 and the chamber's post-PM qualification. The timing points to the change, but the data doesn't confirm the cause.
- Whether the eight held lots should be dispositioned or reworked. Only an engineer can sign that in the MES, and I haven't changed any holds.
- Whether chamber C should stay in production until the rate is back inside the limits.

Sources: `fabwatch etch --runs 30`, `fabwatch events`, `fabwatch lots`, as of 27 Nov 2026 07:45.

Totals over the eight weeks: Columbus 14,300, Reno 14,700, Dallas 14,500. The 28 Dec week is the trough at 2,100 units across all three DCs.
